title: 45 nm Minimum Thickness with 360 nm QW Initialization
scientific_hypothesis: Raising the minimum layer thickness from 20 nm to 45 nm eliminates numerical convergence issues caused by ultra-thin layers, while quarter-wave initialization at 360 nm (center of UV stopband) provides a physically meaningful starting point that improves optimization stability and final target score.
design_principle: Quarter-wave stack design centered at the primary suppression wavelength (360 nm), with bounded thickness constraints that prevent numerically problematic thin layers while maintaining sufficient design freedom for dual-stopband optimization.
proposed_topology: 36-layer alternating Ta2O5/SiO2 stack on fused silica substrate, air incidence, starting with Ta2O5 as first layer
design_variables: optimization trajectory with hard clip operator
soft_objectives: maximize average transmittance in 420-700 nm passband
minimize average transmittance in 355-365 nm stopband
minimize average transmittance in 1030-1080 nm stopband
minimize transmittance at 355 nm single wavelength
manufacturing_considerations: minimum thickness 45 nm improves deposition repeatability
maximum thickness 350 nm within standard process capability
36 layers within typical ion-assisted deposition limits
theory_basis: Quarter-wave optical thickness (n*d = λ/4) provides maximum reflectance at design wavelength for alternating high-low index stacks
Minimum thickness constraints prevent numerical instability in transfer-matrix calculations for ultra-thin layers
expected_advantages: Improved numerical stability compared to 20 nm minimum
Better UV stopband performance due to 360 nm QW center
Faster convergence from physically meaningful initialization
known_risks: 45 nm minimum may limit ability to fine-tune NIR stopband at 1030-1080 nm
Quarter-wave at 360 nm may reduce passband transmittance at longer visible wavelengths
execution_request_english: Optimize a 36-layer planar multilayer filter on fused silica substrate with air incidence at 0 degrees, unpolarized light. Materials: alternating Ta2O5 (high index) and SiO2 (low index), starting with Ta2O5. Layer thickness bounds: 45-350 nm per layer. Initialize all layers to quarter-wave optical thickness at 360 nm (Ta2O5: 360/(4*n_Ta2O5), SiO2: 360/(4*n_SiO2)). Use gradient_thickness optimizer with hard clip operator enforcing 45 nm minimum during first 50% of optimization epochs. Objective: maximize weighted score combining (1) high average transmittance in 420-700 nm, (2) low average transmittance in 355-365 nm, (3) low average transmittance in 1030-1080 nm, (4) low transmittance at 355 nm. Spectral grid: 1 nm spacing from 350-1100 nm. Report best_target_score, valid_candidates, tightest_margin, and thicknesses_nm for all candidates. Canonical user controls: incidence angles 0 degrees. polarization unpolarized. wavelength intervals 355-355 nm, 355-365 nm, 420-700 nm, 1030-1080 nm. soft objectives: high average transmittance in 420-700 nm; low average transmittance at 355 nm; low average transmittance in 355-365 nm; low average transmittance in 1030-1080 nm. behaviors to suppress or avoid: high transmittance at 355 nm; high transmittance in 355-365 nm; high transmittance in 1030-1080 nm; high loss in 420-700 nm. manufacturing constraints: maximum 36 layers; layer thickness range 20-350 nm.
revision_reason: Raised minimum thickness from 20 nm to 45 nm per feedback directive to address numerical convergence issues observed in iteration_01. Changed QW center from 350 nm to 360 nm (center of UV stopband) for better physical alignment. Implemented hard clip operator for first 50% of epochs.
